title: Finite Admixture Models: a Bridge with Stochastic Geometry and Choquet Theory: the growth rate of the expected number of identifiable admixture components (Theorem 3)
author: Michele Caprio, Sayan Mukherjee
work: Finite Admixture Models: a Bridge with Stochastic Geometry and Choquet Theory
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the growth-rate theorem for the expected number of identifiable admixture components, printed as Theorem 3 of "Finite Admixture Models: a Bridge with Stochastic Geometry and Choquet Theory" (source0.tex lines 421--433, source label growth), delivered together with the article's own complete proof at source0.tex lines 1909--1913, which sits detached in the article's appendix under the heading Proof of Theorem 3 and is bound to the statement here. The theorem is the article's first main result, announced in its abstract (the growth rate of the expected number of identifiable components is found by stochastic convex geometry) and listed in its section on main results as the first of three. It states that for points sampled iid uniformly on the unit simplex the expected number of extremal points of their convex hull, which the article identifies with the number of identifiable admixture components, equals J/(J+1)^{J-1} (log n)^{J-1} plus an error of order (log n)^{J-2} log log n, and consequently that the normalised expectation converges to the constant c(J) = J/(J+1)^{J-1}. The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span and consists of the two steps the theorem needs: it quotes the sharp asymptotic expansion of the expected number of vertices of the convex hull of n points sampled uniformly in a convex polytope P of R^d, namely tau(P)/((d+1)^{d-1}(d-1)!) (log n)^{d-1} + O((log n)^{d-2} log log n), from the two cited results (Reitzner's Theorem 6 and Barany-Buchta's Theorem 5, which the article cites at the point of use and which the retained context also flags), and then verifies that the hypotheses hold for the article's own model, since the unit simplex is a convex polytope in R^J, and computes the only quantity the constant depends on, the number of towers of the simplex, tau(Delta^{J-1}) = (J-1)! J. Substituting gives (J-1)! J / ((J+1)^{J-1} (J-1)!) = J/(J+1)^{J-1}, which is exactly the displayed constant of the theorem, and the second display follows by dividing by (log n)^{J-1}. Every step of the reduction and every hypothesis check is in the retained span, the constant is computed rather than asserted, and the only external inputs are the two named published theorems. The argument is rated H2: the statement is a research result that required recognising that a finite admixture model's identifiable components are the extremal points of a random polytope in the simplex, and the count tau(Delta^{J-1}) = (J-1)! J is a genuine verification, but the proof itself is a short and complete reduction to two deep published theorems rather than an independent technical development, so it is not rated H3. It is nevertheless the strongest claim in the article whose proof the article itself writes out in full and whose dependencies are all retained here: the article's other main results either repeat the same reduction pattern (its Theorems 4, 5 and 8), or are propositions whose proofs the article disables inside conditional-false blocks (its proofs of the apeirogon theorem and of the extremal-posterior theorem), or are stated without proof.
